KareenaKapoor Khan

करीना कपूर खान

Her speech planet sits at full strength. Twenty-five years of famously unfiltered interviews later, the chart checks out.

21 SEP 1980 · MUMBAI

TL;DR

Mercury is exalted. So is the mouth that comes with it.

In Vedic astrology Mercury runs speech, logic and wit. In Kareena Kapoor Khan's birth chart Mercury sits in Virgo — the one sign where it's exalted, the strongest a planet can be.
She's spent 25 years as one of Hindi cinema's most quotable, least-filtered interviewees — clipped-and-recirculated soundbites, blunt takes on pay and pregnancy, none of it an accident if you read the placement.

It's not a lone signal either. Sun and Saturn sit in the same sign as Mercury — three planets crowded into one house of the zodiac, a real, computed Virgo stellium. And right now, for the first time in her life, one planet is running both the big chapter of her chart and the small one inside it, at the same time.

2000–2007 · THE ARRIVAL

A star-family debut that still had to prove itself

Refugee → Jab We Met 7 years, one range upgrade
  • Debuted opposite Abhishek Bachchan in Refugee (2000), then the poster-girl blockbuster run of Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001) as "Poo" — a role that turned into a template other actresses still get compared to.
  • Then the pivot nobody expected from a fourth-generation star kid: Chameli (2003) and Omkara (2006), playing a sex worker and a rustic seductress. Jab We Met (2007) fused both sides into the performance still called her best.
🔭 Rahu mahadasha (1991–2009). Rahu is hunger and reinvention — even from inside a film dynasty, this stretch was about proving the name wasn't the whole story.

The tea ☕

Everything you're actually here for

Three storms, all public record. What the chart says about the pattern behind them — not the gossip, and not a verdict on anyone.

🪞 The body-image firestorm, 2007–08
What's public

Around Tashan (2008) she became the industry's poster case for an ultra-thin "size zero" look, publicly criticised as setting an unhealthy standard for young fans.

She later spoke openly against extreme dieting and worked with a nutritionist — pushing back on the very frame that had made her a case study.

What the chart hints

Landed deep in her Rahu stretch. Rahu is obsession and a public gaze fixed somewhere it shouldn't be.

A spotlight fixed on her body rather than her work tracks with a classic Rahu-era story.

💍 A wedding that drew backlash for the wrong reasons
What's public

Her October 2012 marriage to Saif Ali Khan, a Hindu–Muslim union, drew a wave of communal commentary online and in parts of the press.

Neither of them engaged with it directly. They've now been married for well over a decade, with two children.

What the chart hints

This sits right at the start of Jupiter — the expansion planet, which also governs marriage.

Read plainly, the chart's take on the period is warm; the backlash says more about the commentary than the placement.

👶 Working — and getting trolled — through two pregnancies
What's public

She kept public appearances and film commitments visibly pregnant in both 2016 and 2020–21, and returned to promotion and workouts soon after each birth.

The choice drew sustained "bad mother" trolling alongside real admiration, especially online.

What the chart hints

Both births sit inside the same Jupiter stretch that governs children and growth.

The chart doesn't separate "praised" from "criticised" — it just marks the period as her most expansive. The discourse is public opinion, not the chart's business.

Being straight with you: none of the above is a legal or criminal matter — it's public discourse about a very public person. We're naming the pattern the chart shows, not passing judgment on any of it.
Certified range arcs

Two arcs the industry didn't expect

From "Poo" to Chameli in three years flat

  • Debuted as the poster-glam heroine of Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001) — a role some critics wrote off as pure gloss from a star-family debutante.
  • Within two years took an award-tipped turn as a sex worker in Chameli (2003), then Omkara (2006) — author-backed, unglamorous parts nobody expected from her.
  • By Jab We Met (2007) she'd fused both sides into the performance still cited as her career-best.

🔭 The chart bit: her Rahu mahadasha, tail into what became Jupiter. Rahu is reinvention under pressure — proving a name wrong, in public, repeatedly.

Leading films in her 40s, after two pregnancies, when the industry usually moves on

  • Hindi cinema has a well-documented pattern of writing off actresses' box-office pull past 35, especially post-motherhood.
  • She had two sons, in 2016 and 2021, kept working through both pregnancies, and returned to lead and ensemble roles each time.
  • Crew (2024), a female-led heist comedy released when she was 43, was one of that year's biggest hits.

🔭 The chart bit: the back half of Jupiter running into Saturn. Saturn is endurance — the planet that keeps showing up long after everyone assumed you'd stopped.

Astrology, but make it make sense

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

It's a photo of the sky from the exact spot and second you were born. Where each planet was sitting, frozen — that's the whole idea behind a birth chart.

Vedic astrology says that snapshot describes the raw material you were handed — not your fate, your starting kit.

Hers: 21 September 1980, Mumbai. Sun in Virgo, Moon in Capricorn, Mercury exalted in Virgo. Those three carry most of this page.
LESSON 02

Nine of them. Think of them as nine departments, each running one part of a life.

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it's comfortable and signs where it struggles. Same planet, wildly different output depending on where it lands.

  • Exalted (★) — the single best sign for that planet. Full power, nothing fighting it.
  • Own sign — home ground. Comfortable and reliable.
  • Debilitated — the worst sign. Still works, just against friction.
  • Neutral — in between, which is most planets in most charts.
Her scorecard: one planet exalted (Mercury), nothing debilitated, everything else neutral. A quietly strong chart — no placement actively fighting itself, and one planet sitting right at its ceiling.
LESSON 04

Dashas — why timing is the whole game

This is the bit most people have never heard of, and it's where the real story usually is.

Your life splits into long stretches, each one run by a single planet. Fixed order, fixed lengths, and which one you start in is decided by exactly where the Moon was at birth. The technical name is dasha.

Her stretches, computed:
Moon (1980–84) → Mars (84–91) → Rahu (1991–2009) → Jupiter (2009–2025) → Saturn (2025–2044, current)

Rahu covers her debut and the range-proving years. Jupiter covers the biggest hit of her career, her marriage and both her sons. Saturn just started.
LESSON 05

Sub-periods — the chapters inside the chapter

A nineteen-year stretch is too blunt to be useful, so each one splits again into sub-periods, each handed to a different planet. That's how astrologers get from "this decade" to "this year".

Her current sub-period: Saturn, running from 25 June 2025 to 28 June 2028 — inside her Saturn mahadasha, which also started 25 June 2025. Same planet, big chapter and small chapter, at once. That specific overlap is rare enough to be worth calling out on its own.
LESSON 06

What her birth time can — and can't — unlock

A chart has two halves: the signs, which only need the date, and the houses, which need the exact minute, because the rising sign changes roughly every two hours.

A birth time for her is publicly published — 08:39, sourced to Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai. That's a hospital-adjacent record, meaningfully more reliable than the astrology-book guesses common for older Bollywood birth data. But it has never been graded by the Rodden rating system professional researchers use to certify a birth time as verified.

So here's the line we're drawing: the published time is solid enough to fix her exact nakshatra pada and give day-accurate dasha transitions — both of which are genuinely what a birth time is for. It is not, on this page's standard, solid enough to publish a lagna (rising sign) or any house-based claim, including a manglik verdict. Any site giving you her "7th house" or "career house" to the degree is using a source held to a lower bar than this one.
LESSON 07

So — is Kareena Kapoor Khan manglik?

The most-asked astrology question about almost any married Indian celebrity, and the honest answer here is a shrug with a reason attached.

Manglik status depends entirely on which house Mars sits in — 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th. Houses need a Rodden-grade birth minute, and hers doesn't clear that bar yet (Lesson 06).

What we can say: her Mars sits in Libra, a neutral placement, and that holds regardless of the house question. Whether it lands in a manglik house genuinely can't be answered from what's publicly verifiable — and she's been married to Saif Ali Khan since 2012, which is a longer run than most manglik predictions survive anyway.
LESSON 08

How to actually read that chart square

The grid earlier on this page is a South-Indian chart, the easiest of the three regional styles to learn because the signs never move.

Twelve boxes around the edge, one per zodiac sign, always in the same places. Pisces top-left, then clockwise: Aries, Taurus, Gemini along the top, and so on. Memorise the ring once and you can read any South-Indian kundli for the rest of your life.

Try it: scroll back up and find the box marked VIR. Three symbols sit in it — that's the stellium, and now you can see for yourself why it's real and not just marketing copy.
LESSON 09

Aspects — planets shouting across the chart

A planet doesn't only affect the sign it sits in. It also throws influence at the sign directly opposite — astrologers call this an aspect, and every planet gets at least this one, sign-for-sign, regardless of houses.

Hers: Moon and Ketu sit together in Capricorn, staring directly across the wheel at Venus and Rahu, who sit together in Cancer — an exact opposition axis, computed and real. Instinct and detachment on one side, charm and hunger on the other, each fully visible to the other.
LESSON 10

Retrograde and combust, without the drama

Two words that get thrown around a lot and sound far worse than they are.

Retrograde means a planet appears to move backwards across the sky — an optical effect of Earth overtaking it, not an actual reversal. Rahu and Ketu are shown retrograde by definition, always, for every chart on earth — that's normal, not a red flag specific to her.

Combust means a planet sits very close to the Sun and gets lost in its glare, traditionally read as dimming its strength. That needs exact degrees, which this build doesn't carry, so we're not claiming any combustion here rather than guess.

Hers: nothing flagged as retrograde beyond the routine Rahu/Ketu pair, and no combustion claimed without the degree data to back it. Anyone asserting a specific combust planet for her from sign-level data alone is guessing.
LESSON 11

What this can and can't tell you

Worth being blunt, since this page has spent a while treating a chart as a serious object.

  • It can describe tendencies, and it can time long stretches — that part is arithmetic, and two astrologers with the same birth data compute the same periods.
  • It can't tell you what someone will do with those tendencies. Two people with near-identical charts live completely different lives.
  • It definitely can't give exact dates for a diagnosis, a divorce, or an exam result — anyone who does is guessing with confidence.
The honest framing: a chart is a description of the raw material and the weather. It is not a script, and nothing on this page should be read as one.
